title: Snoutrix POC: traffic shape, SLA & benchmark plan
summary: Discovery/POC scoping call to map Snoutrix's conversational inference workload, agree on success criteria (p99 latency under 350ms for 95% of traffic, throughput for 600 QPS burst, fidelity parity vs prod), and define benchmark plan and timeline for a 3-week pilot. Redwood AE+SE covered hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs, KV caching effects, and data residency / SOC2 concerns. Action items and next steps captured at end.
next_steps: Redwood to share benchmark template and sample load script by 2026-11-16
Snoutrix to provide 7-day representative traffic logs (anonymized) by 2026-11-18
Schedule benchmark kickoff (2 hours) the week of 2026-11-23
Prep contact: Omar to approve SSO access and test account by 2026-11-20
action_items: Marcus Nguyen — prepare candidate model variants and expected throughput table — due 2026-11-16
Daniel Reed — export anonymized traffic log (7 days) and token histogram — due 2026-11-18
Lena Park — send Redwood SOC2 & network diagram artifacts + pricing ballpark — due 2026-11-14
Priya Mehta — confirm success KPIs and stakeholders for pilot (POC internal sign-off) — due 2026-11-17
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-13 15:30 UTC | Duration 58m | Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Nguyen (Redwood SE), Omar Ruiz (CTO, Snoutrix), Daniel Reed (Eng Manager), Priya Mehta (Product Lead), Ryan (SRE), Ally (Legal joined 00:42)

[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro — I'm Lena, AE — Marcus is our SE who will run the bench part. Snoutrix team — maybe quick intros?
[00:12] Omar: Omar here, CTO. We run conversational support agents across web and mobile. Our peak QPS hits during promos, uh, so we need to understand burst handling.
[00:22] Daniel: Dan, eng manager, mainly owning infra and orchestration. we'll be running pilot in our staging VPC.
[00:30] Priya: Priya, product, I'll own success metrics and org sign-off.
[00:35] Marcus: good to meet you all. quick preview of agenda: map traffic shape, token distributions, define latency SLOs, propose benchmarks and timeline.

Summary/Context
[00:48] Lena: high level, Snoutrix cares about latency tail, cost, and model fidelity. you mentioned earlier you evaluate outputs against current in-house model; correct?
[00:55] Priya: yeah, fidelity parity is key — if responses degrade we can't roll out. also data residency — our legal team insists on audit logs and SSO for any test accounts.
[01:06] Omar: also isolation — we may need dedicated capacity for certain endpoints, but we're open to hosted if latencies and guarantees check out.

Traffic & workload characterization
[01:20] Marcus: can you walk through current QPS and concurrency? avg vs peak? and request/response token lengths?
[01:28] Daniel: avg steady is ~75 QPS, concurrency around 40, but during campaigns we spike to 600 QPS for 10-15 minutes. typical input tokens 80–120, outputs 40–180 depending on conversation. there's a long tail because some chat sessions do multi-turn summarization.
[01:45] Marcus: cool, that helps. do you have a histogram of tokens or sample logs? even approximate percentiles are useful (p50/p90/p99 length).
[01:55] Daniel: we can extract that — I'll pull a 7-day sample. note: some requests include attachments metadata which inflates tokenization unpredictably.

Latency and SLOs
[02:08] Priya: product asks for p95 under 200ms and p99 under 350ms for the interactive widget. if can't meet p99, we need graceful fallbacks.
[02:20] Marcus: that's ambitious at high QPS, particularly for larger output sizes. we typically see p99 expand with token length and KV cache misses. are you ok with defining SLO tiers? e.g., interactive endpoints p95 200ms/p99 350ms, async batch endpoints looser.
[02:36] Omar: yes let's tier them. interactive top priority.

Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
[02:44] Lena: discuss tradeoffs: Hosted API gives fastest onboarding but shared pools — we provide performance profiles and fallbacks. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools for isolation and consistent throughput. Private (VPC/on-prem) supports strict controls and audit logs.
[02:59] Ryan: for pilot we need VPC peering and SAML SSO. also encryption with our KMS for keys.
[03:06] Marcus: VPC peering and KMS integration supported; there is a short setup time. note that dedicated capacity reduces p99 jitter at high concurrency.

Benchmarks & success criteria
[03:20] Marcus: propose bench plan: 1) replay anonymized 7-day traffic to reproduce natural burst patterns, 2) synthetic stress tests for steady-state at 75 QPS and spike runs to 600 QPS for 15 minutes, 3) token-size bucketed tests (small/medium/large outputs) to measure p50/p95/p99.
[03:40] Marcus: success criteria — fidelity within X% of baseline on eval set (we'll co-design prompts and scoring), p99 below 350ms for interactive 95% of replayed traffic, no more than 1% error rate, and throughput sustainment during 600 QPS bursts with graceful degradation.
[03:56] Priya: what's fidelity within X% mean? we need a clear metric.
[04:00] Marcus: we usually use BLEU/ROUGE-like or embedding-similarity with human spot checks. often requirement phrased as "no more than 10% drop in MRR/intent classification" — we can tailor to your metrics.
[04:12] Priya: ok, let's aim for embedding cosine >= 0.92 on our eval prompts and no critical regressions.

Technical deep-dive (SE)
[04:22] Marcus: a couple of notes: caching (prefix/K V cache) reduces tokens for multi-turn conversations but only helps if session affinity is preserved. continuous batching improves throughput at cost of small latency tradeoffs. quantization choices affect latency and fidelity.
[04:40] Daniel: on session affinity — our front-end uses sticky sessions; should map well. for KV cache, can Redwood honor per-session KV reuse in dedicated pools?
[04:50] Marcus: yes, we support session-scoped KV cache; it does change memory footprint per process. for dedicated sizing we'll estimate kv cache memory based on token window.

Mis-transcription/interruption
[05:05] Speaker 1: (inaudible) ...
[05:08] Lena: sorry, Ally from legal just popped in; Ally, quick hi?
[05:11] Ally: hi, quick Q on logs retention and audit exports — we need 1 year of audit logs for compliance.
[05:18] Lena: Redwood can provide audit logs and we have a compliance package; I'll send SOC2 and retention options.

SLA and fallbacks
[05:29] Marcus: for SLA, we can offer dedicated-backed SLO commitments for dedicated customers. Hosted API has published performance profiles but not the same contractual uptime/latency guarantees.
[05:41] Omar: what happens on capacity loss — auto-fallbacks?
[05:44] Lena: yes, we have routing fallbacks to smaller model variants or cross-region failover depending on policy. tradeoff: lower-cost/low-latency fallback models may have different fidelity.

Timeline and pilot scope
[05:55] Lena: propose 3-week pilot: week 0 (setup & data handoff), week 1 run replay benchmarks and initial tuning, week 2 extended stress tests and fidelity evals, then wrap with findings and recommended prod footprint.
[06:12] Daniel: that timeline works. we need to align with our change freeze near 2026-12-10, so finish pilot by 2026-12-08 ideally.
[06:20] Lena: noted — we'll prioritize to hit that window.

Pricing and procurement notes (brief)
[06:27] Priya: ballpark cost for dedicated for pilot?
[06:30] Lena: we'll send a ballpark estimate; exact pricing depends on model size/quantization and reserved hours. we'll include both hosted test-run pricing and dedicated pilot estimate.

Recap & next steps
[06:44] Lena: recap: Redwood to share benchmark template, Marcus to prepare candidate model table, Snoutrix to provide traffic logs and token histograms, legal artifacts exchange for SOC2 and VPC setup. schedule kick-off next week.
[06:58] Omar: sounds good. Daniel will send the logs.
[07:02] Priya: we'll confirm internal OK for the 3-week window.

[07:10] Lena: thanks all. we'll follow up with calendar invites and the artifact links. bye.

End of transcript. Note: occasional transcription errors — "K V cash" instead of KV cache; "Redwood Dedicate" in one sentence.
